acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A FETCH FAILURE IS NOT AN EMPTY REGISTRY -- DISTINGUISH THEM AT THE SEAM. Three states must be separable and each must be exhibited: served-empty (a valid 200, renders 'no satellites'), fetch failed (renders an error/unknown state, NEVER 'no satellites'), served-populated.
acceptance.invocation: node scripts/ui-smoke.mjs positioning <out>.png --port 5175 --fixtures fx-{populated,empty,failed}.json --click Satellites ; sha256sum on the three PNGs
acceptance.output_evidence: THREE STATES EXHIBITED AND SEPARATED BY HASH, not by my reading of the images: populated cf9e542541dddd2e (9 real books) / empty e02b1764dfb1fd5b (blue 'No satellites to show') / failed 92225d65f302069f (red 'could not be loaded'). MECHANISM: the states are separated AT THE READ SEAM where the difference is still visible -- the fetcher raises, so anything reaching the adapter as [] is a SERVED empty; the render then selects its copy from the QUERY STATUS and never from the emptiness, which cannot tell the two apart.
acceptance.denominator: 3 states declared by the criterion, 3 exhibited, 3 distinct sha256.

[]` at the call site is 'nothing fetched yet' (loading, or the query disabled in another mode), NOT a fallback -- whether an empty set means 'no satellites' or 'the read failed' is decided by the QUERY STATUS. And the axis FAILS TOWARD 'could not load': an UNEXPLAINED absence (settled, not errored, no data) is deliberately read as fetch-failed rather than as an empty registry, because of the two things it could mean only one is safe to assert.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: as_of NON-NULL ALWAYS, including on the empty set -- a null RAISES. The adapter unwraps .books from { books: SatelliteBook[], as_of }; SatelliteBook.code is the CANONICAL NAME verbatim.

acceptance.output_evidence: THE RAISE FIRES, AND THE TEST DISCRIMINATES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The fixture carries a null as_of together with all NINE VALID BOOKS. WITHOUT the raise it is byte-indistinguishable from `populated`; WITH it, byte-IDENTICAL to a transport failure -- sha256 92225d65f302069f == the fetch-failed render, and distinct from both empty and populated. mutant.description: TWO, AND THEY TEST DIFFERENT THINGS. (1) TYPECHECKER: a deliberate `const __probe: number = "not a number"` planted in the NEW file gave TS2322 rc=2; the file was restored and verified byte-identical by `diff -q`, and the clean re-run gave rc=0. Without this the rc=0 is indistinguishable from a cached-skip, which is a live hazard here because `tsc -b` is a project-references build. (2) THE as_of-NULL FIXTURE IS THE STRONGER MUTANT AND IT IS A MUTATION OF THE INPUT, NOT THE CODE: it carries all NINE VALID BOOKS with a null as_of, so it could have failed in EITHER direction -- rendering as `populated` if the raise were absent, or as a failure if present. It renders byte-identical to a transport failure. A test that can only fail one way proves less than one that can fail two.
mutant.expected: The assertion must FAIL against the mutated input/code and PASS against the true one. For the render set, a state that cannot be told from its neighbour by hash is an assertion that was never tested.
mutant.observed: FIRED. The planted TS2322 gave rc=2 and named the new file; the restore was verified byte-identical by `diff -q` and the clean re-run gave rc=0. The as_of-null input-mutant rendered sha256 92225d65f302069f -- byte-identical to the fetch-failed render and DISTINCT from populated cf9e542541dddd2e, so it discriminated in both available directions.

determinism.method: The four render states were captured on separate runs of the same instrument against fixed fixtures and compared by sha256; the failed/as_of-null pair reproduced byte-identical hashes across independent invocations, and the other states reproduced distinct ones. The served-artifact comparison is a sha256 equality between the S3 object body and the route response, not a size or status-code inference.
determinism.observed: STABLE. Four render states captured on separate invocations against fixed fixtures; failed and as_of-null reproduced identical sha256 across independent runs, the others reproduced mutually distinct ones. The served-vs-object comparison is a sha256 equality, not a size or status-code inference.

declared_exclusions.item: Removing the adapter's default second parameter
declared_exclusions.reason: The ruled seam shape is USE the seam, do not redesign it. Removing a default changes the adapter's contract for every caller -- a contract act, not a seam act. Surfaced as a standing hazard instead (see surprises).
DT lane, Rule 19 / SAT-f-3, and held at Andrew's word. Not this lane's and not a condition of this TO.

surprises: OBSERVATION / INERT -- THE ADAPTER'S SECOND PARAMETER KEEPS ITS DEFAULT (= SATELLITE_REGISTRY, the empty constant). A NEW call site that omits the registry silently reproduces the EXACT defect this TO fixed, and nothing fails: no compiler error, no runtime error, just a page rendering 'no satellites' while the producer runs correctly. THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS THE BAD ONE -- the omission is TYPED-SILENT and presents as the wrong-but-plausible reading this TO exists to eliminate. INERT because there is exactly one call site today and it is correct; it ARMS when a second appears. The remedy shape (make the parameter required, so omission becomes a COMPILE error) is named and NOT ruled -- it is a contract change spanning every caller, and picking it inside a wiring TO would be widening this lane's scope on its own authority.

BLOCKING / ARMED, disarmed by owner -- FOUND AS ARM 1 OF THIS SEAT'S OWN AUTH CONTROL, filed by 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z as Z-S16. An `opal-capital` caller MUST supply ?firm= or the router 400s before resolving a bucket (index.mjs:227-241), while modeAccess.ts:118 puts INTERNAL_FIRM_ID in the satellites allowlist. So Opal staff -- including Andrew, whose smoke test is D4's completion bar -- SEE the Satellites pill and the fetch behind it returns 400. This seam handles it honestly (red 'could not be loaded', never 'no satellites'), so it is a product gap rather than a defect in this fix. Shape ruled by 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z and remediated under ETFS_SATELLITES.TO-9-DE.

OBSERVATION -- THE RELAYED WIRE SHAPE WAS WRONG. The route path reached this seat as /api/scoped/advisor-intelligence/platinum/satellites/registry.json. shared-advisor-router/index.mjs:95 declares SATELLITES_PREFIX = '/api/scoped/satellites/', a DEDICATED prefix on a Rule 24(iii) intent-coherence ruling. Building against the relay would have stood up a SECOND ROUTE. Caught by reading the router source before wiring; 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~S hit the same thing independently from the serving side. The correction is written into the new file's own header, so the next reader cannot repeat it -- a correction in an inbox reaches whoever was on the thread; a correction in the file reaches whoever opens the file.
